header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec>`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/status_reads_sync.txt and
drives the REAL liveness pass (`status_store_liveness`), not a copy of it:
the witness is a statement list and the assertion is the per-statement
`live` vector the backend consumes. `store` is a single-target literal
assign (a definite status store); `read` is a `test` whose operand text
carries `$?`. Where the source answers differently from the model, the
test records the source, and its note says so.

pins.note: `store; store; read` -- only the store the read observes (and the read's own exit store) stay live.
`read; store; store` -- nothing reads the first store, so only the last (the exit code) survives.
`read; store; read` -- the second read observes the store between them.
`store; store` with no read at all: only the exit code's store is live.
A bare `exit` observes the current status, so the store before it stays live.
A statement that does not definitely store but whose nested list reads `$?` before its own first store: that read observes the preceding store, so nothing is dropped.
The dead store in `store; store` is unobservable: index 0 of the vector is false.
The KEPT store in `store; store` is the one the process exit observes, so `sys.exit(__sh_rc)` is exact.
`read; store` -- a read with nothing live before it reads the register's INITIAL value, so the initialiser cannot be dropped.

The empty program: no stores and no readers. DIVERGENCE, recorded as the source has it: the model's `live` is the empty vector, while `status_store_liveness` answers None ('keep every store') before it scans. The two agree in effect -- with no statement there is no store to drop -- and None is the conservative side.
One statement that reads and stores: its store is the exit code, so it is live.
